gloss: to grow older; to age; to accumulate years

definitions.gloss: to grow older; to age; to accumulate years
definitions.explanation: To advance in age over time. A softer, more dignified way to express aging than direct words like 'to get old.' Often carries a positive or neutral nuance of gaining experience and maturity.

examples.japanese: {年|とし}を{重|かさ}ねるごと⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{味|あじ}→味：00826_aji⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}てくる→出てくる：29121_detekuru⟧。
examples.english: With each passing year, more character emerges.

examples.japanese: {年|とし}を{重|かさ}ねて⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{元気|げんき}→元気：00696_genki⟧で⟦いたい→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: I want to stay healthy even as I grow older.

examples.japanese: {年|とし}を{重|かさ}ねて⟦{初|はじ}めて→初めて：02932_hajimete⟧⟦{分|わ}かる→分かる：00463_wakaru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There are many things you can only understand after growing older.

notes:
Literally 'to pile up years.' A euphemistic and respectful way to describe aging. The verb ⟦{重|かさ}ねる→重ねる：02039_kasaneru⟧ (to pile up, to accumulate) emphasizes the gradual accumulation of years and experience.

USAGE:
Preferred over ⟦{老|ふ}ける→老ける：16742_fukeru⟧ (to age, to grow old) or ⟦{年|とし}→年：00486_toshi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧ (to get older) in polite contexts because it avoids negative connotations. Often used in reflective or philosophical contexts about life.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {年|とし}を{重|かさ}ねるごと⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧: with each passing year
- {年|とし}を{重|かさ}ねて⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧: even as one ages
- {年|とし}を{重|かさ}ねた⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧: an older person (respectful)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{年|とし}→年：00486_toshi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧: to get older — more neutral, everyday expression
- ⟦{老|ふ}ける→老ける：16742_fukeru⟧: to age, to grow old — can sound negative
- ⟦{歳月|さいげつ}→歳月：13198_saigetsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{経|へ}る→経る：13876_heru⟧: for years to pass — more literary
